affirmation-is-not-love.metaDescription: Therapeutic culture taught us that to love someone is to confirm them.

qa.question: Is Affirmation the Same as Love?
qa.answer: Therapeutic culture taught us that to love someone is to confirm them. But real love wills the good of the other, and sometimes that means telling the truth they do not want to hear. A pastor on the difference, and why it costs.

authority-we-traded-for-authenticity.metaDescription: Somewhere in the last few decades a sentence changed shape in the Christian mouth. The old sentence was 'the Bible says.'

qa.question: Is the Bible the Final Word, or Am I?
qa.answer: Somewhere in the last few decades a sentence changed shape in the Christian mouth. The old sentence was 'the Bible says.' The new one is 'I feel like God is.' We thought we were gaining freedom. We were changing kings.

cheap-grace-left-hand.metaDescription: Bonhoeffer's cheap grace is usually aimed at the easy-believism of the right.

conscience-outsourced-to-party.metaDescription: We talk about the church captured by the political right. A pastor on the conscience we handed our tribe without ever signing the papers.

qa.question: Should a Christian Follow a Political Party?
qa.answer: We talk about the church captured by the political right. The left's version is harder to see, because the left believes it is the side that thinks for itself. A pastor on the conscience we handed our tribe without ever signing the papers.

deconstruction-without-reconstruction.metaDescription: The exvangelical wave got the diagnosis right. The wounds are real and the church earned most of them.

qa.question: What Happens After You Deconstruct Your Faith?
qa.answer: The exvangelical wave got the diagnosis right. The wounds are real and the church earned most of them. But deconstructing your faith and never rebuilding is not freedom, it is an empty house, and empty houses do not stay empty.

right-side-of-history.metaDescription: "The right side of history" is the most successful piece of secular theology of our age, and the American church swallowed it whole.

the-sin-we-stopped-naming.metaDescription: Progressive Christianity recovered structural sin and called it justice.

when-justice-becomes-a-gospel.metaDescription: Is social justice biblical? Yes, which is exactly why it makes such a convincing god.

nostalgia-is-not-the-kingdom.metaDescription: The longing for a lost Christian America feels like faith and works like idolatry.

qa.question: Was America Ever Really a Christian Nation?
qa.answer: The longing for a lost Christian America feels like faith and works like idolatry. It is the mirror image of the progressive worship of the future, a moment on the calendar mistaken for the kingdom of God.

six-verses-we-memorized.metaDescription: A tribe does not have to delete a single verse to edit the Bible. It only has to decide which ones get printed in bold.

strongman-theology.metaDescription: A frightened church always asks for a king. We are praying the same prayer. The elders did not ask for a tyrant. That is the part everyone misses.

the-flag-in-the-sanctuary.metaDescription: How the American flag came into church sanctuaries, what civil religion is, and how Scripture separates loving your country from worshiping it.

qa.question: Should Churches Have an American Flag in the Sanctuary?
qa.answer: The flag beside the pulpit arrived through war and grief, not through a vote or a theology. Loving your country is a Christian virtue; the question is whether the sanctuary still teaches which loyalty is final.

the-persecution-we-invented.metaDescription: A church that ran the culture for a thousand years lost the room and called it persecution.

qa.question: Is the American Church Really Being Persecuted?
qa.answer: A church that ran the culture for a thousand years lost the room and called it persecution. Here is what that word costs us, and what the actual persecuted church would say if we let them speak.

the-third-temptation.metaDescription: In the wilderness, Satan offered Jesus all the kingdoms of the world if he would bow. Power was always the temptation.

two-kingdoms-one-pledge.metaDescription: You cannot pledge ultimate allegiance twice. Allegiance. It is not a soft word.

qa.question: Can You Pledge Allegiance to Two Kingdoms?
qa.answer: You cannot pledge ultimate allegiance twice. A pastor on the two-kingdoms tradition, the cost of following a crucified King, and why the line between Caesar and Christ runs straight through the American Christian's chest.

when-the-pulpit-became-a-precinct.metaDescription: A church does not have to endorse a candidate to become a precinct. It only has to make the tribe feel at home and the outsider feel watched.

six-lenses-that-distort-the-bible.metaDescription: You think you read the Bible plainly. Here is how to see the glass before it edits the text.

christendom-is-ending.metaDescription: What Christendom was, from Constantine and Theodosius to Westphalia and America's Protestant consensus, why it is ending, and what faith looks like after.

qa.question: What Is Christendom, and What Comes After It?
qa.answer: Christendom was the settlement that made Christianity the default of Western life, from Constantine to the American Protestant consensus. It is ending. Christianity is not, and confusing the two leaves the church grieving the wrong loss and reaching for the wrong remedies.

exile-is-not-the-end.metaDescription: What Jeremiah 29 meant to the exiles of 597 BC, how Peter and Augustine read it, and whether American Christians can honestly call themselves exiles.

qa.question: Are American Christians exiles at all?
qa.answer: The modern revival of the word came from more than one direction. Stanley Hauerwas and William Willimon's Resident Aliens (1989) marked Christendom's end with a small scene from Willimon's youth, a Sunday evening in 1963 when the Fox Theater in Greenville, South Carolina, opened in defiance of the old blue laws. They called the church a colony, an island of one culture in the middle of another, whose first political task is to be the church. Lee Beach's The Church in Exile (2015) developed the exile reading into a practical theology for congregations after Christendom.

the-numbers-behind-the-decline.metaDescription: The statistics about the dying church get quoted in two directions, apocalypse and denial, and both are usually wrong.

what-dies-when-christendom-dies.metaDescription: Not everything that is dying in the church deserves to be mourned. When something large dies, the first grief is indiscriminate.

witness-without-power.metaDescription: The early church conquered the Roman Empire without a single seat in its government.

discipling-people-out-of-fear.metaDescription: Political capture runs on fear, and you cannot argue a frightened person back to peace.

pastoring-a-captured-congregation.metaDescription: Your people are being discipled forty hours a week by a screen that knows them better than you do.

qa.question: How Do You Pastor a Church Addicted to Cable News?
qa.answer: Your people are being discipled forty hours a week by a screen that knows them better than you do. A working pastor on shepherding a congregation whose first language has quietly become cable news.

preaching-to-a-divided-room.metaDescription: Half your room is braced for you to betray them and the other half is hoping you will.

the-last-nonpartisan-in-the-room.metaDescription: Everyone wants to know which side you are on, and refusing to say it costs you something real.

when-elders-are-loyal-to-a-party.metaDescription: The capture that endangers a church most is not in the pews. It is on the board.

burnout-is-not-a-badge.metaDescription: We turned exhaustion into a virtue and then wondered why our best men kept collapsing. The empty man is not the faithful man.

the-loneliest-room-in-the-church.metaDescription: The fullest building in town has one room where a man sits alone with everything he is not allowed to say.

the-pastor-nobody-checks-on.metaDescription: We built a vocation where the man who asks everyone how they are gets asked by no one. Here is how the grammar got that way, and what it takes to break it.

when-the-calling-costs-more.metaDescription: No one lied to us about the calling. They just never finished the sentence about the bill, and the second invoice has names and dates the first one didn't.

why-pastors-quit.metaDescription: Most pastors do not quit on the bad day. They quit on the ordinary one, after a long erosion no one watched happen.

emotional-labor-in-marriage.metaDescription: What emotional labor and the mental load really are, why one spouse ends up carrying them, why children deepen the gap, and what Scripture asks of both.

qa.question: Why Does One Spouse Carry the Whole Mental Load in Marriage?
qa.answer: The heaviest work in many marriages is not the chores but the watch: the anticipating and remembering that leaves no trace when it is done well. Children multiply it, and Scripture has always called it work that both spouses owe.

the-resentment-in-your-marriage.metaDescription: What resentment in marriage means, when a grievance is fair and when it turns to bitterness, and how Scripture moves from honest speech to forgiveness.

the-slow-drift-that-ends-marriages.metaDescription: Why couples drift apart and end up like roommates: the old sin of acedia, the modern soulmate marriage, and how Scripture calls spouses back to attention.

what-silence-costs-a-marriage.metaDescription: Why the silent treatment wounds a marriage, when silence protects or listens instead, and what Scripture, Bonhoeffer and Gottman teach about talking again.

qa.question: Where are you?
qa.answer: The first question God asks a human being in Scripture is asked of a man who has gone silent. "But the LORD God called to the man and said to him, 'Where are you?'" (Genesis 3:9). God isn't lost. The man is. And God doesn't accept the silence as the new arrangement. He comes looking, with a question rather than a charge, which leaves room for an answer, and he walks through the hedge of leaves and trees not to shame the man but to draw him back into speech.

what-the-bible-says-about-submission.metaDescription: Ephesians 5 read in context: mutual submission, headship defined by the cross, both main Christian views, and why submission never requires enduring abuse.

qa.question: What Does the Bible Say About Submission in Marriage?
qa.answer: Ephesians 5 begins a sentence earlier than it is usually quoted, and its heaviest command falls on the husband. Read whole, it gives no one a license to dominate and no one permission to hide.

when-you-married-someone-you-no-longer-r.metaDescription: Why spouses become strangers, especially once the kids leave, what growing apart does and does not mean, and why the marriage vow was made for this season.

qa.question: I Don't Recognize My Spouse Anymore. Is the Marriage Over?
qa.answer: The stranger across the table is not proof the marriage failed. Both of you changed, as every vow assumed you would, and the question is whether you will learn the person who is actually there, including the one in the mirror.

discipline-without-domination.metaDescription: What biblical discipline means: paideia in Ephesians and Hebrews, the rod in Proverbs read as wisdom, the spanking debate, and correcting without anger.

family-devotions-authentic.metaDescription: How to do family devotions and teach kids to pray and read the Bible: what Scripture asks of a home, what history shows, and what tired parents can keep.

how-to-talk-kids-faith-doubt.metaDescription: How to pass on faith to your kids when you have doubts: what Scripture says, what research on handing down faith found, and why honesty outlasts theater.

raising-kids-who-think.metaDescription: How to answer kids' hard questions about God: why Scripture expects children to ask, what the catechisms knew, and why owned questions outlast recitation.

raising-sons-manhood.metaDescription: What biblical manhood means for raising sons: the domineering and diminished counterfeits, the virtue tradition, and Christ's strength under control.

teenager-losing-faith.metaDescription: Your first instinct will be to win the argument. The argument is not the thing your teenager is testing. You are.

the-pastors-kids-are-watching.metaDescription: Your congregation hears your sermons. Your children watch the drive home.

the-weight-of-what-you-model.metaDescription: Why kids learn faith from their parents' example: imitation in Scripture, Bandura and Girard on modeling, hypocrisy, and why a parent's repentance matters.

the-work-nobody-watches.metaDescription: The culture calls mothering a waste of a mind. The church hands it a carnation one Sunday a year and loads it like a mule the other fifty-one.

can-you-have-faith-and-doubt.metaDescription: Can a Christian doubt and still believe? What Scripture does with doubters, how doubt differs from unbelief, and why certainty is not the same as faith.

qa.question: Can You Have Faith and Doubt at the Same Time?
qa.answer: Doubt is a question asked from inside trust; unbelief is a settled refusal to trust. The church lost many of its most honest people by confusing the two, and by mistaking a modern demand for certainty for the confidence Scripture actually commends.

constantines-bargain.metaDescription: Much of what people leave when they leave the faith is not the faith at all.

depression-or-the-dark-night.metaDescription: On depression, the dark night of the soul, and the line no one should have to find alone. Fifteen years of pastoring keeps sending me the same two people.

excavation-not-demolition.metaDescription: Demolition and excavation use the same tools, the pry bar, the shovel, the refusal to respect a wall just because it is standing.

what-if-we-are-wrong.metaDescription: The question shows up at night: what if the whole thing is a story we told ourselves? A faith that cannot survive that question was never faith.

qa.question: What If Christianity Is Wrong?
qa.answer: The question arrives uninvited, usually at night: what if the whole thing is a story we told ourselves? A faith that cannot survive the question was never faith. It was shelter.

when-fear-rewrites-theology.metaDescription: Fear does not announce itself as fear. It tells you the worry is wisdom.

why-does-god-feel-far-away.metaDescription: Feeling that God is far away is not a conclusion you reasoned your way to. It is the weather of our age. A pastor who came from atheism on why.

qa.question: Why Does God Feel So Far Away?
qa.answer: The sense that God is distant is not a conclusion you reasoned your way to. It is the weather of an age. A pastor who came to faith from atheism on disenchantment, the buffered self, and why the thinness you feel is the ceiling of a house rather than the edge of the world.

the-weight-that-stays.metaDescription: You were promised the grief would lift. It did not lift. The literature of grief is full of stages, and the stages imply a destination.

when-god-is-silent-and-the-room-is-empty.metaDescription: Why does God feel silent? Isaiah's hidden God, the lament psalms, Job, the dark night, the hiddenness argument, and Holy Saturday, when God lay in a grave.

the-faith-once-delivered.metaDescription: What Jude meant by the faith once delivered, how the creeds of Nicaea and Chalcedon confess Scripture, and why America's no creed but the Bible fails.

the-trinity-plainly.metaDescription: It sounds like a math problem the church flunked: one God, three persons. It was never math.

qa.question: How Can God Be Three and One?
qa.answer: It sounds like a math problem the church flunked: one God, three persons. It was never math. It is the church's best attempt to say everything true about a God who showed up in person.

what-the-creed-leaves-out.metaDescription: If you only knew Christians from the internet, you would think they agree on nothing.

why-christians-recite-creeds.metaDescription: Standing in a room of strangers, reciting words written before your country existed, sounds like the opposite of real faith.

qa.question: Why Would Anyone Recite a 1,700-Year-Old Creed?
qa.answer: Standing in a room of strangers, reciting words written before your country existed, sounds like the opposite of real faith. It is closer to the truth than 'just me and my Bible' ever was.

why-the-incarnation-matters.metaDescription: What is the incarnation? John 1, Philippians 2, the councils from Nicaea to Chalcedon, and why God becoming man matters for sin, suffering and the body.

easter-is-not-a-day.metaDescription: Easter as the church's oldest feast: Passover and Pascha, the Vigil, the fifty days, why East and West differ on the date, and the truth about Eostre.

qa.question: Eostre, Eggs and Rabbits: Is Easter Pagan?
qa.answer: Every spring someone posts that Easter is a pagan festival with a cross painted on it, sometimes a skeptic who thinks Christianity is borrowed mythology, sometimes a Christian who thinks the faithful shouldn't keep the holiday. Both assume the name and customs tell you what the feast is. The claim deserves a patient answer, because part of it is true.

what-is-advent.metaDescription: What Advent is, how it grew from fasts in Gaul and Rome's four Sundays, and why the season before Christmas waits for Christ's return as well as his birth.

qa.question: Does a Christian Have to Keep Advent?
qa.answer: Many faithful Christians don't keep Advent, and their reasons deserve their strongest form. The Puritan objection to the calendar as a whole is traced in the essay on the church year. The objection to Advent in particular runs like this. The New Testament commands watchfulness but never a season of it. "Stay awake" was spoken about every hour, and to give the return of Christ a season implies the rest of the year is off duty. The free-church Christian, Baptist or independent, would say the whole of life is Advent, and a liturgical season risks turning a daily readiness into an annual mood.

why-lent.metaDescription: Why Christians keep Lent and fast: the forty days in Scripture, early church fasting, the Reformers' objections, and how to fast wisely and safely.

why-the-church-has-a-calendar.metaDescription: What the church calendar is, how it grew from Israel's feasts and early Christian practice, and what its seasons from Advent to Ordinary Time form in us.

qa.question: Is the Church Calendar Biblical?
qa.answer: Many Christians who don't keep the church year decline it on principle, and the principle deserves to be stated as its defenders would state it. God alone may say how he's to be worshiped, and the New Testament appoints one holy day, the Lord's day. Everything else in the calendar is human invention, however old and lovely, and the apostles warned against binding consciences with it. Paul was alarmed at the Galatians: "You observe days and months and seasons and years!" (Galatians 4:10, ESV).

the-table-that-divides.metaDescription: The one meal Jesus left to hold his people together has become the thing that most visibly keeps them apart. A newcomer notices this fast.

what-happens-at-communion.metaDescription: A small piece of bread. A sip from a cup. Christians have argued for centuries about what it means and almost never about whether it matters.

qa.question: What Actually Happens at Communion?
qa.answer: A small piece of bread. A sip from a cup. Christians have argued for centuries about what it means and almost never about whether it matters. Here is what is going on when the church eats.

why-baptism.metaDescription: What baptism is, from Romans 6 to the Didache, and why churches split over infant or believer's baptism, immersion or sprinkling, sacrament or ordinance.

qa.question: Sacrament or Ordinance: What Does the Water Do?
qa.answer: Beneath the debate over who and how lies a third question, older and in some ways deeper: what the water actually does. Augustine gave the classic definition in his Tractates on the Gospel of John: "Accedit verbum ad elementum, et fit sacramentum," the word comes to the element, and it becomes a sacrament. A sacrament, on this account, is a visible sign through which God gives what he has promised.

why-christians-confess-out-loud.metaDescription: Saying your worst out loud, to another person, in plain words, almost everything in us resists it.

why-faith-uses-physical-things.metaDescription: If Christianity is about the spirit and the soul, why is it so obsessed with stuff, water, bread, oil, wine, a body on a cross?

silence-and-solitude.metaDescription: What the desert fathers, Benedict's Rule, Elijah and Jesus teach about silence and solitude, why we flee them, and how solitude differs from loneliness.

angels-demons-and-the-unseen.metaDescription: As a materialist this was the easiest thing in the Bible to mock, and later the thing I had understood least. Angels, demons, an unseen order.

are-miracles-believable.metaDescription: Hume's argument against miracles at full strength, the replies of Lewis, Swinburne, Earman and Keener, and what the Gospels say miracles are for.

can-you-be-good-without-god.metaDescription: Yes, unbelievers can be good. The harder question is where morality comes from: Plato's Euthyphro, Kant, Darwin, Nietzsche and the law on the heart.

can-you-lose-your-salvation.metaDescription: Can you lose your salvation? Five Christian views at full strength, Hebrews 6 and John 10 read in context, and where assurance of salvation truly rests.

christian-sexual-ethic.metaDescription: Is the Christian view of sexuality homophobic? Genesis, Jesus, Romans 1, the strongest affirming and traditional cases, and the church's failures.

qa.question: Is the Christian View of Sexuality Homophobic?
qa.answer: The church has often treated gay people with contempt, and that has to be confessed first. But the historic Christian ethic is a vision of the body that asks the same costly thing of everyone, and it deserves to be weighed at full strength beside its best critics.

christianity-and-islam.metaDescription: How Christianity and Islam differ on the Trinity, Jesus, the cross, revelation and grace, and whether Christians and Muslims worship the same God.

qa.question: Christianity vs Islam: What Is the Real Difference?
qa.answer: Christianity and Islam are neither the same faith nor strangers. They agree that God is one, great and merciful, and they part over whether he has shown his face in Jesus, crucified and raised.

christians-and-abortion.metaDescription: What the Bible and the historic church teach about abortion, the strongest pro-choice arguments answered, the hard cases, and grace for the wounded.

did-god-command-genocide.metaDescription: Did God command genocide in Joshua? The herem texts, the skeptic's case, ancient war rhetoric, Rahab, Marcion and the cross, and what still stays hard.

did-the-resurrection-happen.metaDescription: The historical case that Jesus rose: the early creed in 1 Corinthians 15, the empty tomb and women witnesses, and the strongest skeptical replies weighed.

divorce-and-remarriage.metaDescription: Biblical grounds for divorce and remarriage: Moses, Jesus, and Paul read in context, four Christian views, and why no view requires staying in danger.

qa.question: What Does the Bible Say About Divorce and Remarriage?
qa.answer: Asked whether a man could divorce his wife for any cause, Jesus tightened the law of Moses and named an exception in the same breath. Read in context, the texts are harder than the culture wants and more merciful than the church has often been.

does-god-actually-exist.metaDescription: Aquinas, Leibniz, the kalam and Anselm's proof, the objections of Hume, Russell, Mackie and Oppy, and which God the arguments would reach if they worked.

qa.question: Why is there anything at all?
qa.answer: The most famous arguments begin from the plainest fact available: something exists. They are usually lumped together as "the cosmological argument," as though there were one, and much of the confusion in popular debate comes from that lumping. There are at least three distinct arguments here, and they stand or fall on different premises.

faith-and-gender-identity.metaDescription: Before it is a debate, it is a person. The church has owed both of them something for a long time, and mostly sent an argument instead.

qa.question: What Does the Church Owe Transgender People?
qa.answer: Before it is a debate, it is a person. A teenager who cannot stand to be in the body they woke up in, and a mother in the parking lot who does not know how to keep her child alive and keep her faith at the same time. The church has owed both of them something for a long time, and mostly sent an argument instead.

faith-and-science.metaDescription: How the war between science and Christianity was invented, what historians found about Galileo, Darwin and Scopes, and what science cannot answer.

how-to-read-genesis-one.metaDescription: How Genesis 1 is built, what it answered in the ancient world, six ways Christians read the days, and the historical Adam debate, stated fairly.

if-god-is-good-why-suffering.metaDescription: Why does a good God allow suffering? Epicurus, Plantinga, Rowe's fawn, Job and the cross, and why the answer must never be used on the grieving.

is-faith-irrational.metaDescription: What faith means in Scripture, Clifford's charge that it is belief without evidence, and the replies of William James, Plantinga, Aquinas and Pascal.

is-faith-just-wishful-thinking.metaDescription: Feuerbach, Marx, Nietzsche and Freud said God is a wish. The replies of Vitz, Lewis and Plantinga, and why Christian hope is not the same as optimism.

is-hell-eternal.metaDescription: It is not whether there is a hell that keeps people awake. It is whether it stops.

qa.question: Is Hell Forever, or Does It End?
qa.answer: It is not whether there is a hell that keeps people awake. It is whether it stops. There is a difference, and every grieving heart knows it, between a God who lets a soul finally cease and a God who keeps it alive forever so it can go on burning.

is-jesus-really-the-only-way.metaDescription: Is Jesus the only way to God? John Hick's pluralism at full strength, Rahner and Newbigin, Acts 4:12 and John 14:6 in context, and those who never heard.

qa.question: Is Jesus Really the Only Way?
qa.answer: For most of my life I was an atheist, and of all the things the church claimed, that Jesus is the only way struck me as not merely improbable but obscene. But the parable of the blind men and the elephant cannot survive one question: who is telling it?

just-war-and-pacifism.metaDescription: Two Christians read the same Sermon on the Mount. One picks up a rifle to stop a slaughter. One lays the rifle down and lets them kill him first.

meaning-without-god.metaDescription: The atheist is not the miserable nihilist the church invented to feel better. He builds real, loving, meaningful lives.

qa.question: Can a Life Mean Anything Without God?
qa.answer: The atheist is not the miserable nihilist the church invented to feel better. He builds real, loving, meaningful lives. The question is not whether he can make meaning. It is whether meaning you make can hold you when you stop believing in it.

personhood-in-the-age-of-ai.metaDescription: The machine can now do most of what I once called the mark of a mind. It can talk, reason, even say it feels.

qa.question: What Makes Us Human in the Age of AI?
qa.answer: The machine can now do most of what I once called the mark of a mind. It can talk, reason, even say it feels. So I have to say honestly what in me it can never be, and why that is not the thing I would have guessed.

predestination-and-free-will.metaDescription: Predestination vs. free will from Augustine to Dort, Wesley and Barth: both views at full strength, Romans 9 in context, and what the creeds leave open.

qa.question: Predestination vs. Free Will: What Does the Bible Teach?
qa.answer: The church has argued for sixteen centuries over whether God chooses us or we choose him, and the creeds never closed the question. Both answers are stronger than their cartoons, and both send the frightened soul to the same place.

the-atheist-in-the-pulpit.metaDescription: A pastor who was an atheist with real reasons tells the honest story of what changed his mind, slowly and against his own preference, and what it cost him.

the-cost-of-following.metaDescription: Every invitation to believe you have ever received was trying to sell you something, and you were right to smell it.

was-jesus-just-a-good-teacher.metaDescription: The polite modern verdict on Jesus is that he was a great moral teacher, nothing more. C.S. Lewis said that was the one thing he never left open to us.

qa.question: Was Jesus Really Just a Good Teacher?
qa.answer: The polite modern verdict on Jesus is that he was a great moral teacher, nothing more. C.S. Lewis said that was the one thing he never left open to us. The trilemma gets attacked, fairly, so here it is pressure-tested against the best objections.

what-new-atheists-got-right.metaDescription: I owned the books. I underlined them, I argued from them, and I would have followed all four horsemen off a cliff.

why-didnt-the-bible-ban-slavery.metaDescription: When I was an atheist this was the argument I kept at the top of the list.

qa.question: Why Didn't the Bible Just Ban Slavery?
qa.answer: When I was an atheist this was the argument I kept at the top of the list. If the book were really from a good God, somewhere in all those pages it would say four words: own no human being. It never does. I no longer think that ends the conversation, but I understand why I thought it did.

why-trust-the-bible.metaDescription: Can you trust the Bible? An honest look at manuscripts, the Dead Sea Scrolls, how the canon formed, the Gospels as history, contradictions and inerrancy.

qa.question: Who decided which books are in the Bible?
qa.answer: The second piece of the folklore is more dramatic. In Dan Brown's The Da Vinci Code (2003), a character explains that Constantine commissioned a new Bible, that Jesus was voted into godhood at the Council of Nicaea in 325, and that earlier gospels portraying him as a mortal man were suppressed. Millions of readers took it as history. Nicaea was called to settle the Arian controversy over whether the Son is fully God, and its creed and canons say nothing about which books belong in the New Testament.

women-in-ministry.metaDescription: Can women be pastors? Both views stated at full strength, with Genesis, Deborah, Phoebe, Junia, 1 Timothy 2, church history, and why it is second-order.

the-bible-without-the-marketing.metaDescription: The flat, all-or-nothing Bible you were handed is a fairly recent invention. Inspiration is older.

the-historical-jesus-without-the-shortcu.metaDescription: What historians agree about Jesus: the Roman and Jewish sources, the case against the myth theory, the three quests, and where historical method stops.

what-following-this-actually-costs.metaDescription: The honest closer. No altar call. A faith that asks for everything is at least not selling you something cheap.

what-secular-explanations-still-have-to-.metaDescription: Consciousness, reason, morality, fine-tuning, the church's rise and our longing for more: what naturalism still must explain, and why it isn't a gap.

does-god-change-his-mind.metaDescription: The Bible says God does not change. The Bible also says God 'relented' and 'changed his mind.'

qa.question: Does God Change His Mind?
qa.answer: The Bible says God does not change. The Bible also says God 'relented' and 'changed his mind.' Both are right, and the resolution is not a dodge, it opens onto the strangest and most stabilizing thing anyone has ever said about God.

is-god-in-control.metaDescription: We say God is in control and then watch a world that looks anything but controlled.

qa.question: If God Is in Control, Why Doesn't It Feel Like It?
qa.answer: We say God is in control and then watch a world that looks anything but controlled. The gap between the doctrine and the headline is where a lot of faith quietly dies. The tradition's answer is not glib, and it does not ask you to call the wreckage good.

the-god-who-hides.metaDescription: If God is real and wants to be known, why is He so often silent? The felt absence of God has driven people out of faith and kept others from entering it.

qa.question: Why Does God Hide?
qa.answer: If God is real and wants to be known, why is He so often silent? The felt absence of God has driven people out of faith and kept others from entering it. The tradition does not explain the silence away. It does something stranger, it makes a home in it.

qa.question: Is it wrong to be angry at God?
qa.answer: The Christians who say you shouldn't be angry at God aren't fools, and their case deserves the form they'd sign. Anger is a moral judgment; to be angry at someone is to hold that he has done wrong. God cannot do wrong. He is the standard of righteousness, not a party measured against it. So anger at God is always misdirected, a creature putting the Creator in the dock, and the fitting response to loss is Job's on the first day: "The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD" (Job 1:21, ESV).
